## Objective
- Refine and validate the playable Kamikaze Robots remake, focusing on physics, damage and head-launch behavior, course difficulty, upgrades, and AI competitiveness.

## Requirements
- Stack bounce power after consecutive feet-first landings following at least one air spin; reset immediately on non-feet-first contact.
- Body-first impacts remove arms before legs, with stamina resistance; good landings wear limbs slowly.
- Eject the head on the next contact after losing all four limbs, launching in the body’s current orientation; Explosion scales launch speed and distance, and the head can win by crossing the finish.
- Match terrain collision to visible ground, including bumps and slopes.
- Lengthen and harden courses while preserving names, visual style, menus, and objectives.
- Slow upgrade progression and keep AI competitive; retain repeatable cleared-course chip awards.
- Preserve “HOLD TO BRAKE,” responsive controls, and clear damage/power-reset feedback.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing TypeScript/Vite project and procedural course system.
- Keep course names and themes; increase course length and terrain variation through the existing level-generation table.
- Interpolate the same 5-unit terrain samples for collision and rendering.
- Upgrade prices: 1 chip for levels 1–2, 2 for 3–5, 3 for 6–8, and 5 thereafter.
- Cleared-course replay chip awards remain repeatable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Increased generated course lengths, slopes, bump counts, and terrain heights.
- Added bounce stacking/reset state, limb wear/loss, and head-launch physics/rendering.
- Aligned terrain drawing and stroke endpoint sampling.
- Added HUD feedback for limb count, bounce multiplier, power reset, best spin/height objectives, and head-based race position.
- Updated `README.md` with controls, features, scope notes, and tuning references.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` pass after the latest AI edit.
- Targeted Node checks passed for bounce stacking/reset, limb-loss order and stamina, head finish crossing, and repeatable awards.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in-browser, especially damage/power feedback, menus, controls, and head-based finishing.
- Continue tuning and validating AI competitiveness on later courses.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run browser validation using the available Playwright runtime at `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright` and inspect desktop/mobile captures.
2. Test in-game bounce stacking/reset, limb-loss sequence and stamina resistance, head launch/finish crossing, replay awards, upgrade progression, and AI behavior.
3. Tune any gameplay failures; ad hoc simulation showed mixed results on courses 5, 15, and 29.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.ts`: terrain, physics, collision, damage, AI, rendering, and race awards.
- `src/main.ts`: upgrade prices, HUD, menus, objectives, and progression.
- `README.md`: controls, features, and tuning notes.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: browser capture workflow and Playwright runtime configuration.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. `git status --short` showed modified `README.md` and untracked project files including `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `src/`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `tsconfig.json`.
- Node-based ad hoc simulation produced mixed AI/player outcomes: course 5 had an AI finish, course 15 had an AI finish while the player head did not finish, and course 29 had a player finish; results varied with simulation setup.
- A local `import('playwright')` failed with `Cannot find package 'playwright'`; the capture script loads Playwright from `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright` instead.

## Objective
- Refine and validate the playable Kamikaze Robots remake, focusing on physics, damage and head-launch behavior, course difficulty, upgrades, and AI competitiveness.

## Requirements
- Stack bounce power after consecutive feet-first landings following at least one air spin; reset immediately on non-feet-first contact.
- Body-first impacts remove arms before legs, with stamina resistance; good landings wear limbs slowly.
- Eject the head on the next contact after losing all four limbs, launching in the body’s current orientation; Explosion scales launch speed and distance, and the head can win by crossing the finish.
- Match terrain collision to visible ground, including bumps and slopes.
- Lengthen and harden courses while preserving names, visual style, menus, and objectives.
- Slow upgrade progression and keep AI competitive; retain repeatable cleared-course chip awards.
- Preserve “HOLD TO BRAKE,” responsive controls, and clear damage/power-reset feedback.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing TypeScript/Vite project and procedural course system.
- Keep course names and themes; increase course length and terrain variation through the existing level-generation table.
- Interpolate the same 5-unit terrain samples for collision and rendering.
- Upgrade prices: 1 chip for levels 1–2, 2 for 3–5, 3 for 6–8, and 5 thereafter.
- Cleared-course replay chip awards remain repeatable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Increased generated course lengths, slopes, bump counts, and terrain heights.
- Added bounce stacking/reset state, limb wear/loss, and head-launch physics/rendering.
- Aligned terrain drawing and stroke endpoint sampling.
- Added HUD feedback for limb count, bounce multiplier, power reset, best spin/height objectives, and head-based race position.
- Updated `README.md` with controls, features, scope notes, and tuning references.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Targeted Node checks passed for bounce stacking/reset, limb-loss order and stamina, head finish crossing, and repeatable awards.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in-browser, especially damage/power feedback, menus, controls, and head-based finishing.
- Continue tuning and validating AI competitiveness on later courses.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run browser validation with the available Playwright runtime and inspect desktop/mobile captures.
2. Test in-game bounce stacking/reset, limb-loss sequence and stamina resistance, head launch/finish crossing, replay awards, upgrade progression, and AI behavior.
3. Tune any gameplay failures; simulations have shown mixed AI/player outcomes on later courses.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.ts`: terrain, physics, collision, damage, AI, rendering, and race awards.
- `src/main.ts`: upgrade prices, HUD, menus, objectives, and progression.
- `README.md`: controls, features, and tuning notes.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: browser capture workflow.
- `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright`: Playwright runtime used by the capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. `git status --short` showed modified `README.md` and untracked project files including `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `src/`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `tsconfig.json`.
- Targeted mechanics checks pass, but browser validation has not yet been completed.
- Simulations showed mixed results on courses 5, 15, and 29; a faster AI jump-start variant improved some outcomes but was not adopted.
- `import('playwright')` fails from the project directory; `/usr/bin/chromium` is present and the capture script resolves Playwright from its runtime directory.
